title: Gmail reads the whole thread for you #shorts
description:
Gmail will read a fifty-message thread and give you back one paragraph.

At the top of every thread there is a control that says Summarize this email. Google's own help page puts it plainly: the feature is available to all Gmail users globally, on a work, school or personal account. Most people have never once pressed it.

Two settings control it. One is Smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet. The other is Smart features in Google Workspace. Both of them start switched off if you live in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland or Japan. Nobody switched them off. You were simply never given them.

So open Gmail. Go to Settings, then General, and turn both of those on. Then find the thread you have been scrolling past — dozens of replies with a decision buried somewhere in the middle — and press the button. You get the key points and the replies that mattered, in one paragraph, at the top of the thread. You read that, and then you answer.

Sources: Google, Gmail Help, "Catch up on email threads with AI Overview conversation summaries" (support.google.com/mail/answer/16561387) and "Learn about smart features and controls" (support.google.com/mail/answer/15604322). Read 31 August 2026.

#gmail #google #gemini #ai #aitools
